verdict.rationale: Airbyte's docs define incremental sync as pulling only data changed since the previous sync. Its CDC docs describe Airbyte tracking its current position in database logs to capture inserts, updates and deletes, and a hands-on user reports that after the initial sync Airbyte continued syncing incrementally from saved state. A community question about hard-delete handling is an open question, not a contradiction. Missing for 10: explicit first-party docs on cursor-field selection and how state is persisted for standard (non-CDC) incremental connections, and documented hard-delete handling in cursor-based incremental mode.

support.subject: As a data engineer, syncs move only new and changed records — cursor and state management handled for me, not full reloads

citations.quote: An incremental sync is a sync which pulls only the data that has changed since the previous sync

A consumer of these log files (such as Airbyte) can read these logs while keeping track of the current position within the logs in order to read all record changes coming from DELETE/INSERT/UPDATE statements.
A sync mode governs how Airbyte reads from a source and writes to a destination.
'tricked' Airbyte into thinking it had done the first sync. After that, it continued to sync happily.
